title: Proteomic Analysis of ROCK Inhibitor-treated ARPE-19 Cells
projectDescription: Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) inhibitors are highly present in different ocular tissues, and upregulation of ROCK pathway has been shown related to the pathogenesis of multiple ocular disorders, including glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration (AMD). However, the effect of ROCK inhibitor on AMD is still unknown. The protein profile changes in human retinal pigment epithelium (ARPE-19) cells after two days treatment with a ROCK inhibitor were studied using label-free Zeno SWATH acquisition. These results provided significant data of key protein candidates underlying the effect of ROCK inhibitor. Using the sensitive label-free mass spectrometry approach with data-independent acquisition (SWATH-MS), we established a comprehensive ARPE-19 proteome library. This project describes the use of Zeno SWATH MS to examine the underlying biological protein changes following ROCK inhibitor treatment of APRE-19 cells. This knowledge may allow more specific anti-AMD drugs to be developed
sampleProcessingProtocol: Cell pellets were lysed with 50 µl of lysis buffer (5% SDS, 50mM TEAB, pH 7.55) in a 2 mL tissue homogenizing CKMix standard tube. The homogenization process was done in a liquid nitrogen cooling chamber at 5,800 rpm for 30 seconds at 4°C. Cell lysates were centrifuged and the supernatant was collected. Protein concentration was measured using the Pierce™ Rapid Gold BCA Protein Assay Kit according to the user manual.  Protein digestion was done using the S-trap micro spin column protocol. In brief, 50 µg of protein samples were reduced with tris(2-carboxyethyl) phosphine hydrochloride (TCEP) at a final concentration of 5 mM and alkylated with methyl methanethiosulfonate (MMTS) to a final concentration of 20 mM. Phosphoric acid was added to ensure denaturation of the proteins and efficient trapping. S-trap binding buffer was then added, and samples were placed in a micro spin column for centrifugation to trap the proteins. Samples were subsequently washed with the S-trap protein binding buffer. Trypsin (1:10, w/w) was then added and incubated for 1 hour at 47°C for digestion. Samples were then sequentially eluted with 50 mM TEAB, 0.2% formic acid and 50% acetonitrile. These eluents were pooled together and dried in a Refrigerated CentriVap Vacuum Concentrator (Labconco Corporation, USA) at 4°C. Peptides were then resuspended with 0.1% formic acid, and peptide concentration was determined using Pierce™ Quantitative Peptide Assay.
dataProcessingProtocol: With 1ug per injection, each sample was loaded with one technical replicate into a microflow liquid chromatography (LC) system. Specifically, peptides of each sample were loaded into a nanoEase™ M/Z HSS T3 column (100Å, 1.8µm, 300x150mm; Waters Corporation) with a 30-minute gradient elution, which was interfaced with a ZenoTOF™ 7600 mass spectrometer (SCIEX) operating under the ZenoSWATH acquisition protocol with 64 variable isolation windows. For protein identification and quantification, the generated raw ZenoSWATH files (.wiff) were subjected to process using DIA-NN 1.8.1, which matches the sequences using a UniProt (https://www.uniprot.org) FASTA database of the human proteome (UP000005640, accessed in July 2023). The raw ZenoSWATH files was also deposited to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository with the identifier … (to add later on). The resulting main report file of DIANN was integrated into the OneOmics paltform (SCIEX) via PeakView 2.1 (SCIEX) for data quality control and statistical evaluation for features abundance.  The Analytics and Browser of the OneOmics tabs were used to determine the data quality and to assess the differentially expressed proteins (DEPs). The analytical protein list was filtered out with criteria that met a 75% confidence, 0.15 reproducibility, and at least 2 matching peptides. The cut-offs of a DEP were set to a signed fold change (FC) of ≥ 1.3 or ≤ -1.3 (i.e., log2FC ≥ 0.38 or log2FC ≤ -0.38) and p-value < 0.05.
